brief:
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's UN General Assembly speech was crafted primarily for a domestic audience rather than international listeners, Mondoweiss reported. The address conveyed to Israelis that the country need not alter its policies provided it maintains internal unity and confronts global opposition as a bloc.

Netanyahu's framing suggests a strategic pivot toward embracing Israel's isolation on the world stage. The messaging centered on the notion that national survival depends on military strength and domestic cohesion rather than diplomatic accommodation or policy adjustment.
dek: Netanyahu’s speech at the UN General Assembly was not directed at the world, but Israelis. He was trying to convince them that Israel doesn’t need to change, as long as it stands united against the world — and lives by the sword.
title: Netanyahu tells Israelis to accept isolation over change
